text: A digit is one number symbol. We build every number from ten digits.
A numeral is a number written with digits.
The tens place shows how many groups of ten. A ten-bar is the same as ten ones.
The ones place shows how many single gems are left over.
A hundred is ten tens. A hundred-block is made of ten ten-bars.
When we swap ten ones for one ten, that's called regrouping.
Greater than means bigger. The pointy end faces the smaller number.
Less than means smaller. The pointy end faces the smaller number.
Equal means exactly the same amount. Both sides of an equals sign match.
The sum is the answer when we add.
The difference is the answer when we subtract.
A fact family uses the same three numbers. Add and subtract facts live together.
Inverse means opposite. Adding and subtracting undo each other.
An even number can make pairs with none left over.
An odd number has one left over when we make pairs.
An array is a set of objects in rows and columns.
A row goes across, from side to side.
A column goes up and down.
Equal groups have the same number of items in each group.
To multiply means to add equal groups, but faster.
Commutative means the order does not change the answer.
